newsitem.title: USA: Pardon likely for death row dog.
newsitem.headline: Pardon likely for death row dog.

text.p: Gov. Jeanne Shaheen and New Hampshire's Executive Council indicated Thursday they might pardon Prince, the Portsmouth pooch condemned to death.

The 3-year-old Labrador retriever, named Prince, who faces execution for killing a rooster and escaping twice from his cage, received so much publicity that the five-member elected body took time out from approving state contracts and confirming appointments to unanimously approve a resolution asking the town of Portsmouth to seek a pardon hearing immediately.

Prince killed a rooster last May and, as a result, was declared a "vicious" dog by city authorities in Portsmouth. He was supposed to be caged and walked only on a chain, but Prince escaped twice last summer, and under Portsmouth's vicious-dog ordinance, any two-time escapee must be put to death.
A hearing was scheduled for Tuesday. Portsmouth City Attorney Robert Sullivan said he wants to settle out of court.

The case drew international media attention and provoked an outpouring of sympathy for Prince, owned by Margaret Kristiansen, and her son Jeffrey, 5. The veterinarian where the dog was being kept said he will not execute him.

"We all love our pets and if the dog had harmed a child, that would have been a lot more serious. But this is a bird, and there's a question as to whether the punishment fits the crime," Gov. Shaheen said.
